99	
100	```
101	   <GEMM already wrote this PE's partial into the SYMMETRIC slot tr.local(slot_off)>
102	   tr.rendezvous(bar);                         // (A) cross-CTA GridBarrier + cross-GPU nvshmem barrier
103	   tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(tr, slot_off,  // (B) ASCENDING-pe fp32 reduce over peer slots

108	The determinism-critical detail (the A/A/A + fp64-parity requirement): step (B)
109	is the **hand-rolled ascending-pe loop** in `tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order`
110	(already in `tp_transport.cuh`), NOT `nvshmemx_float_sum_reduce` (whose reduction
111	order is unspecified → ULP drift → A/A/A failure). On NVSHMEM the loop reads
112	`tr.peer(slot_off, pe)` which is `nvshmem_ptr(heap_base, pe) + off` — a direct
113	NVLink load/store of peer pe's symmetric slot, summed in fixed ascending order.
114	This is **already the code in the repo** — the math does not change. What §3
115	adds is making `tr.rendezvous(bar)` actually fence across GPUs (today the
116	`NvshmemTransport::rendezvous` exists but §3 hardens its barrier discipline and
117	adds the symmetric-heap quiet/fence the NVLink-load path needs).
118	
119	**(3) How it composes with the hand GridBarrier (cross-RANK vs cross-CTA).**
120	There are TWO barrier systems and they must be nested, never interleaved:
121	- the hand `GridBarrier` (`megakernel_common.cuh`) is **cross-CTA, within one
122	  GPU** (sense-reversing, no cooperative launch);
123	- `nvshmem_barrier_all` / `nvshmemx_barrier_all_block` is **cross-PE (cross-GPU),
124	  device-and-grid-wide** on the NVSHMEM team.
125	
126	The discipline (already sketched in the `NvshmemTransport::rendezvous` comment,
127	hardened in §3): inside `rendezvous(bar)` do `bar.sync()` (all CTAs of THIS GPU
128	arrive) → **exactly one CTA per GPU** crosses `nvshmemx_barrier_all_block()` →
129	`bar.sync()` again (release every CTA after the cross-GPU join). The NVSHMEM
130	barrier must be entered by **one CTA per GPU only**, never concurrently with the
131	GridBarrier spin — otherwise the two barriers deadlock (a CTA spinning on the
132	GridBarrier generation while another waits in the NVSHMEM barrier for it to
133	arrive). §3 adds the `nvshmem_quiet()` (drains outstanding peer stores) BEFORE
134	the cross-GPU barrier so the ascending-pe NVLink loads in step (B) observe every
135	peer's published partial.
136

139	## §2 — THE SYMMETRIC-HEAP ALLOCATION REQUIREMENT (the hard one — forces an allocator change)
140	
141	This is the honest blocker the task asks me to flag. The operands of an
142	NVSHMEM reduce **must live in the NVSHMEM symmetric heap** (`nvshmem_malloc`),
143	NOT in a plain `cudaMalloc` workspace. `nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe)` only translates
144	pointers that were returned by `nvshmem_malloc` (or `nvshmemx_buffer_register`'d)
145	— a raw `cudaMalloc` pointer is NOT a symmetric address and `nvshmem_ptr` returns
146	garbage/nullptr for it.
147	
148	Today the TP slot lives in the **`cudaMalloc`'d workspace**
149	(`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu` → `dec_tc_launcher_scratch` →
150	`cudaMalloc(&s.workspace, ...)`). The TP slot is carved from that same blob (the
151	loopback heap in `tp_loopback_binding.cu` is `at::zeros(...)`, also non-symmetric
152	— fine for loopback, fatal for real NVSHMEM).
153	
154	**⇒ The TP comm slots must be split out of the `cudaMalloc` workspace into a
155	SEPARATE `nvshmem_malloc`'d symmetric region.** Two options:
156	
157	- **Option A (minimal, RECOMMENDED): a small dedicated symmetric TP-slot heap.**
158	  Only the reduce slots need to be symmetric — `tp_heap_stride_floats(ctas_per_pe)`
159	  = `ctas_per_pe * 2 * kTileM * d` floats (§ `tp_layer.cuh::tp_heap_stride_floats`).
160	  At the flagship (d=1600, kTileM=128, one tile/CTA, ~132 CTAs → 132 PEs-worth on
161	  the loopback but on real multi-GPU it is `ctas_per_pe` per PE): the symmetric
162	  region is `nCTA * 2 * 128 * 1600` floats ≈ `132 * 2 * 128 * 1600 * 4 B`
163	  ≈ 216 MB per GPU — allocate via `nvshmem_malloc`, leave the big acts/grad/state
164	  workspace on `cudaMalloc`. This is the smallest blast radius.
165	
166	- **Option B (whole-workspace symmetric):** make the entire `dec_tc_workspace`
167	  symmetric. Simpler call-site math (one base) but wasteful — the acts/grad/state
168	  regions never need cross-PE addressing, and `nvshmem_malloc` is collective
169	  (every PE must call it with the same size in the same order). Not recommended.
170	
171	The allocator change is in `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`
172	(`DecTcLauncherScratch`): add an `nvshmem_malloc`'d `tp_sym_heap` field, populated
173	ONLY on `kEmitComm` (gated `#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)`), pass its base into the
174	kernel via the widened `CommCtx`. On the SingleGPU path the field stays nullptr
175	and the workspace is byte-identical to today (the §6 PTX gate).
176	
177	**Symmetric-heap sizing must be UNIFORM across PEs** (collective allocation):
178	size with the WORLD-max `(T,B,nCTA)` so every PE's `nvshmem_malloc` call agrees;
179	the host plan already knows the global shapes.
180	
181	---
182	
183	## §3 — EDIT 1: harden `NvshmemTransport` in `tp_transport.cuh`
184	
185	The existing `NvshmemTransport` is close but (a) does the cross-GPU barrier
186	without an explicit `nvshmem_quiet()` before it (so a peer's published partial
187	may not be visible to the ascending-pe NVLink load), and (b) does not carry the
188	TP **team** (it uses the global `nvshmemx_barrier_all_block`, which barriers the
189	WHOLE world, not just the TP group — wrong when TP is one axis of a 4D mesh:
190	DP/PP replicas would be dragged into the TP barrier). Both are fixed here.
191	
192	### VERBATIM OLD (copied from `csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_transport.cuh` lines 137–183)
193	
194	```cpp
195	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
196	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
197	//  NvshmemTransport — the REAL device-initiated transport (design §5.2).
198	//  COMPILED ONLY under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 (toolkit on the path). The math code
199	//  path is IDENTICAL to the loopback's; only the address translation + the
200	//  rendezvous scope differ:
201	//    * `heap_base` is an nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC allocation (same offset
202	//      valid on every PE);
203	//    * `peer()` translates via nvshmem_ptr (NVLink direct load/store — the

397	def fixed_order_reduce_scatter_grad(grad_local, ctx, bucket_elems=25_000_000):
398	    """ZeRO-3 fixed-order reduce-scatter: each DP rank ends with the reduced grad for
399	    ONLY its owned flat slice(s), summed in ASCENDING-RANK fp32 order (the §2.7 A/A/A
400	    discipline), averaged by world. Bucketed so the transient gather is bounded at
401	    ~bucket_elems*world floats, NOT total*world (the flagship full-grad all-reduce is
402	    47 GB at total=1.476B × world=8 — this caps it at ~0.8 GB/bucket × 8). world=1 ⇒
403	    returns the owned slice of grad_local unchanged.
404	
405	    Returns a dict {(fs,fe): reduced_grad_slice} keyed by the store's owned flat
406	    ranges, so the sharded apply in [3] indexes it directly. The reduce is over
407	    ctx.process_group (the DP group under 4D — TP/PP peers are NOT summed)."""
408	    torch = _torch()
409	    if ctx.world <= 1:
410	        return {(fs, fe): grad_local[fs:fe].contiguous()
411	                for fs, fe, _, _ in ctx.store.owned()}
412	    import torch.distributed as dist  # noqa: PLC0415
413	    ws = ctx.world
414	    grp = ctx.process_group
415	    out = {}
416	    # Reduce each owned slice with a fixed-order ascending-rank fp32 sum. We gather
417	    # ONLY the bytes covering the union of owned ranges, one bucket at a time, so the
418	    # transient never exceeds bucket_elems*world. (Elementwise-even: one contiguous
419	    # owned slice; tensor-granular: ≤30 slices — both bounded.)
420	    for fs, fe, _ss, _se in ctx.store.owned():
421	        n = fe - fs
422	        seg = grad_local[fs:fe].contiguous()
423	        off = 0
424	        acc = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.float32, device=grad_local.device)
425	        while off < n:
426	            blk = min(bucket_elems, n - off)
427	            gathered = torch.empty(blk * ws, dtype=seg.dtype, device=seg.device)
428	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
429	            dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, seg[off:off + blk].contiguous(),
430	                                        group=grp)
431	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
432	            for r in range(ws):                       # ascending rank — fixed order
433	                acc[off:off + blk] += gathered[r * blk:(r + 1) * blk]
434	            off += blk
435	        acc /= float(ws)
436	        out[(fs, fe)] = acc
437	    return out

205	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,

207	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
208	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
209	        float acc = 0.0f;
210	        #pragma unroll 1
211	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
212	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
213	        }
214	        dst[i] = acc;
215	    }

43	// the buffers are process-lived scratch, recreated only when a larger B needs a
44	// bigger workspace). Zeroed in-kernel (P0) each launch; never freed (one per
45	// device, leaked at process exit like every other cuBLAS/cuDNN handle).
46	struct DecTcLauncherScratch {
47	    int*     g_next = nullptr;        // int [1]
48	    unsigned* g_arrived = nullptr;    // unsigned [1]
49	    unsigned* g_generation = nullptr; // unsigned [1]
50	    float*   workspace = nullptr;     // float [dec_tc_workspace_floats(T,B,nCTA)]
51	    int64_t  ws_floats = 0;
52	    int      dev = -1;
53	};
54	
55	DecTcLauncherScratch& dec_tc_launcher_scratch(int dev, int64_t need_floats) {
56	    static DecTcLauncherScratch s;
57	    if (s.dev != dev) {
58	        // First use on this device (or a device switch — the race is single-GPU,
59	        // but be honest if it ever moves): (re)allocate the counters.
60	        s.dev = dev;
61	        if (!s.g_next)      cudaMalloc(&s.g_next, sizeof(int));
62	        if (!s.g_arrived)   cudaMalloc(&s.g_arrived, sizeof(unsigned));
63	        if (!s.g_generation)cudaMalloc(&s.g_generation, sizeof(unsigned));
64	    }
65	    if (s.ws_floats < need_floats) {
66	        if (s.workspace) cudaFree(s.workspace);
67	        cudaMalloc(&s.workspace, (size_t)need_floats * sizeof(float));
68	        s.ws_floats = need_floats;
69	    }
70	    return s;
71	}

74	// mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc — the WIRED TC launcher. Boundary mirrors the scalar
75	// mega_decoder_real_adamw (dispatch.cpp extern-decls it with the same mirror
76	// types) EXCEPT it takes NO workspace pointer: the TC workspace is a different
77	// size from the scalar nCTA*total partials, so this TU allocates+owns it. `loss_out`
78	// still points into the caller's state[3*total] slot (dispatch reads it back).
79	//
80	// OPTID-GENERIC (owner baseline directive — all 33 cells on L3-TC): the fwd+bwd+
81	// grad-reduction is OPTIMIZER-INDEPENDENT (the same validated wgmma decoder kernel);
82	// ONLY the per-element optimizer TAIL (apply_optimizer<Opt>) differs, and that tail
83	// is the 14/0-apply-parity math already in opt_components.cuh. So this launcher
84	// takes `opt_id` (the OptId int) and dispatches to the matching kernel instantiation
85	// over the SAME state buffer. The state layout is [m | v | extra] (3*total) + loss:
86	//   * lion              uses m only (v/extra unread; bound harmlessly)
87	//   * adamw             uses m, v
88	//   * grokfast/grokadamw use m, v, ema  (ema == the `extra` slice, state + 2*total)
89	//   * neuralgrok        uses m, v, AND a psi-net weight pack the cell supplies in the
90	//                       `extra` slice (kPsiPackFloats floats); st.psi_W1/b1/W2 bind
91	//                       to those offsets, exactly as opt_components.cuh documents.
92	// The STAGED optimizers prodigy (P2.6 global-d) and muon (P2.7 grid-cooperative NS)
93	// ARE routed here: their precompute is an IN-KERNEL phase, so they remain a SINGLE
94	// persistent launch (the cases below). The SAM-coupled SG11/SG15/looksam and SG2 are
95	// NOT — they need a 2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd / a sharpness ABI field / a segmented sort
96	// that this single-launch path does not carry; dispatch.cpp gates them out (and
97	// wiring_check fails them loud with the cited reason). NeuralGrok is wired but its
98	// host-trained amplifier is a separate concern (the race fn gates it).
99	//
100	// ncta_cap: forwarded to the TC launcher (0 = one CTA/SM = full saturation, the
101	// shipped config). The race always passes 0.
102	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
103	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
104	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
105	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,
106	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
107	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
108	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
109	    (void)sizes; (void)offsets;  // TC kernel reads kDecSizes/kDecOffsets directly.
110	
111	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
112	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
113	
114	    int dev = 0;
115	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
116	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
117	    int n_sms = 1;
118	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
119	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
120	    int nCTA = n_sms;
121	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
122	
123	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
124	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
125	
126	    // Re-point the ctx counters at THIS TU's cached counters (dispatch.cpp built
127	    // ctx pointing at its scalar DecoderScratch counters; the TC launcher zeroes
128	    // them per-launch, but they must be the ones this scratch owns so the grid
129	    // barrier is consistent with the workspace).
130	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
131	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
132	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
133	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;  // parameter tensors for reduce+opt phases
134	
135	    // Bind the optimizer state slices. [m | v | extra] over the SAME state buffer;
136	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused
137	    // pointers are never dereferenced). ema/psi-net live in the `extra` slice.
138	    float* const m_slice     = state;
139	    float* const v_slice     = state + total;
140	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
141	    FusedOptState st;
142	    st.exp_avg    = m_slice;
143	    st.exp_avg_sq = v_slice;
144	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
145	    // NeuralGrok psi-net pack (kPsiPackFloats floats at the head of `extra`): the
146	    // cell places [psi_W1 | psi_b1 | psi_W2 | psi_b2] there; bind the device pointers
147	    // so the apply reads real weights (psi_b2 is read on-device from psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
148	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;
149	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
150	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
151	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings. The cell extends the state buffer
152	    // to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init | r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host
153	    // sizes it to >= 4*total + 4; see dispatch.fused_train_step). The `extra` slice
154	    // doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads st.s_track,
155	    // not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA). The
156	    // trajectory anchor p0 (param_init) follows the loss slot; the 3 persisted
157	    // estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init. loss_out points at
158	    // state+3*total (dispatch's loss_slot), so param_init = loss_out + 1.
159	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
160	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
161	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
162	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward): sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM
163	    // direction (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the
164	    // grokfast EMA / Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The
165	    // in-kernel P2.4 phase WRITES it on SAM steps; the apply tail READS it every step.
166	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
167	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu). State
168	    // layout: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
169	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45 precompute; the
170	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
171	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
172	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
173	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
174	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 is read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
175	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45-filled)
176	    {
177	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
178	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
179	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
180	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
181	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
182	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
183	    }
184	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
185	    st.lr = lr;
186	
187	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
188	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
189	    tok.targets   = targets;
190	    tok.B         = B;
191	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
192	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
193	
194	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
195	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
196	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD (no
197	    // silent scalar/adamw fallback — the no-suppression rule). The STAGED/model-coupled
198	    // optimizers are intentionally NOT cases here (they cannot run as a single launch).
199	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
200	        case OptId::AdamW:
201	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
202	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
203	        case OptId::Lion:
204	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
205	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
206	        case OptId::Grokfast:
207	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
208	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
209	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
210	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
211	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
212	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
213	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
214	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
215	        case OptId::Prodigy:
216	            // STAGED global-d: the SAME single persistent launch — the d-estimate
217	            // cross-tensor reduction is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between B2 and P3),
218	            // not a separate launch. st carries param_init/prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/
219	            // beta3; the kernel decays+accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies.
220	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
221	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
222	        case OptId::Muon:
223	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME
224	            // single persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights
225	            // (tok/pos/in_proj/out_proj/ff.0/ff.2/out) is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.7,
226	            // between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a separate
227	            // launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace (dec_tc_muon_floats,
228	            // carved after the Prodigy reduce slots). The persistent momentum buffer is
229	            // the m-slice (st.exp_avg); the 1D/non-2D weights take the AdamW tail in P3
230	            // reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_* group). The
231	            // vit twin (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu) proved this routing.
232	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
233	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
234	        case OptId::LookSAM:
235	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME single
236	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
237	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
238	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
239	            // workspace (dec_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Muon scratch); sam_dir
240	            // persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply tail (P3)
241	            // blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate launch.
242	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
243	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
244	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
245	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (wave-3
246	            // decoder lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward
247	            // (P2.4, sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P2.45,
248	            // mu=rescale·phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL
249	            // in-kernel phases between B2 and P3; the apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step:
250	            // smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in P3. The SAM scratch reuses
251	            // the looksam buffers (dec_tc_looksam_floats); sharpness + the phi pack ride
252	            // the extended state buffer (bound above). NOT a separate launch.
253	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
254	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
255	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
256	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate
257	            // is a host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage;
258	            // the apply tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad
259	            // = g + gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
260	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
261	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
262	        default:
263	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
264	    }

267	// mega_decoder_sg2_tc — the DEDICATED SuperGrok2 TC launcher. SG2 needs the FULL
268	// CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net weight bundle (26 HBM pointers, model-independent) +
269	// per-tensor scalar ARRAYS (alpha/gru_decay/lamb_eff/beta1/bc1/bc2, length P) +
270	// the meta-net state (m/v/mu/slow/gru_state/sharpness), none of which fit the
271	// FusedScalars POD or the generic mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc boundary. So this is
272	// a PARALLEL entry (the generic launcher + the 28 byte-identical cells are
273	// UNTOUCHED). It binds the SG2 state slices, threads the weight bundle + scalar
274	// arrays through FusedOptState's sg2_* fields, and dispatches the OptId::SuperGrok2
275	// kernel instantiation (its P3-SG2 phase runs sg2_meta_stages per tensor: STAGE -1
276	// in-kernel segmented sort → CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply, reading st.sharpness from the
277	// SAM 2nd backward (P2.4, shared with SG11/15)).
278	//
279	// STATE LAYOUT (host sizes it; this carves it):
280	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
281	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
282	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
283	cudaError_t mega_decoder_sg2_tc(
284	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
285	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
286	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,
287	        // SG2 meta-net weight bundle (HBM, fp32, model-independent), in SG2Weights order.
288	        const float* input_proj_W, const float* input_proj_b,
289	        const float* csa_q_W, const float* csa_k_W, const float* csa_v_W, const float* csa_out_W,
290	        const float* csa_compress_w, const float* csa_idx_DQ, const float* csa_idx_K,
291	        const float* hca_q_W, const float* hca_k_W, const float* hca_v_W, const float* hca_out_W,
292	        const float* gru_Wz, const float* gru_bz, const float* gru_Wr, const float* gru_br,
293	        const float* gru_Wh, const float* gru_bh,
294	        const float* peer_query_Ws, const float* prod_keys_A, const float* prod_keys_B,
295	        const float* expert_W1, const float* expert_b1, const float* expert_W2, const float* expert_b2,
296	        // per-tensor scalar arrays (device, length kDecNumTensors).
297	        const float* sc_alpha, const float* sc_gru_decay, const float* sc_lamb_eff,
298	        const float* sc_beta1, const float* sc_bc1, const float* sc_bc2,
299	        // shared scalars + the SAM 2nd-backward gate (SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4
300	        // machinery: rho = perturbation radius, sam_on = every-k SAM-step gate).
301	        float rescale, float beta2, float lr, float wd, float eps,
302	        float rho, float sam_on,
303	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {
304	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
305	    // gru_state spans total*GH (GH=DecSG2Dims::gru_hidden); the layout is fixed by
306	    // the kernel's SG2State carve, so the slices below need no GH arithmetic here.
307	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
308	
309	    int dev = 0;
310	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
311	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
312	    int n_sms = 1;
313	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
314	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
315	    int nCTA = n_sms;
316	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
317	
318	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
319	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
320	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
321	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
322	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
323	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;
324	
325	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
326	    FusedOptState st;
327	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
328	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
329	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
330	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
331	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
332	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
333	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
334	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
335	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
336	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
337	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
338	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
339	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
340	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
341	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
342	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
343	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
344	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;
345	    st.sg2_prod_keys_B = prod_keys_B;
346	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
347	    st.sg2_expert_W2 = expert_W2; st.sg2_expert_b2 = expert_b2;
348	    // per-tensor scalar arrays.
349	    st.sg2_alpha = sc_alpha; st.sg2_gru_decay = sc_gru_decay; st.sg2_lamb_eff = sc_lamb_eff;
350	    st.sg2_beta1 = sc_beta1; st.sg2_bc1 = sc_bc1; st.sg2_bc2 = sc_bc2;
351	    st.sg2_rescale = rescale;
352	    // shared scalars the SG2 phase reads (beta2/lr/wd/eps via FusedScalars fields).
353	    st.beta2 = beta2; st.lr = lr; st.wd = wd; st.eps = eps;
354	    // SAM 2nd-backward gate: SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4 machinery. st.rho is the
355	    // perturbation radius (SG2's sam_rho); st.looksam_sam is the every-k SAM-step gate
356	    // (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sharpness=(g_sam−g)² this step;
357	    // 0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sharpness). On a non-SAM step the cached sharpness feeds
358	    // the meta-net verbatim (eager-faithful).
359	    st.rho = rho;
360	    st.looksam_sam = sam_on;
361	
362	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
363	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
364	    tok.targets   = targets;
365	    tok.B         = B;
366	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
367	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
368	
369	    return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok2>(
370	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
371	}
